canonical_statement: The primary objective was to assess whether nMAS automated heart-failure feature engineering produces structurally valid, rubric-compliant, and clinically coherent patient-level features; downstream predictive performance was secondary.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although downstream predictive performance is reported as a secondary evaluation, the primary objective is to assess whether automated feature engineering produces structurally valid, rubric-compliant, and clinically coherent patient-level features.

canonical_statement: Patients were included if they had a documented heart-failure diagnosis in the source EHR; no additional inclusion or exclusion criteria were applied.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were included if they had a documented heart-failure diagnosis in the source EHR; no additional inclusion or exclusion criteria were applied.

inclusion_criteria: Documented heart-failure diagnosis in the source EHR

canonical_statement: The evaluation dataset contained 500 dummy patient records from an aggregated single-institution cardiovascular cohort modeled on a program serving a minoritized population.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The evaluation dataset consisted of 500 dummy patient records drawn from an aggregated cohort modeled on REDACTED, a cardiovascular program serving a minoritized population.

population.label: Dummy heart-failure records from an aggregated cohort modeled on a single-institution cardiovascular program serving a minoritized population

canonical_statement: Each patient was represented across nine structured EHR tables spanning demographics/core diagnoses, other diagnoses, medications, echocardiography, surgery, internal labs, external labs, ejection fraction, and social history.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each patient was represented across nine structured EHR tables covering demographics, other diagnoses, medication orders, echocardiogram procedures, surgical procedures, laboratory components and external labs, ejection fraction flowsheet entries, and social history (Table 4 in the Appendix).

canonical_statement: Direct patient identifiers were replaced with de-identified identifiers before analysis while clinically relevant information required for feature extraction and phenotyping was preserved.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Direct patient identifiers were replaced with de-identified identifiers before analysis, while clinically relevant information required for feature extraction and phenotyping was preserved.

canonical_statement: The Achievability Agent checks whether available source data support each target feature and reports features with absent required inputs as unsupported rather than inferring values.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The Achievability Agent first checks that the available source data can support each target feature; features whose required inputs are absent are reported as unsupported rather than assigned inferred values.

canonical_statement: Stage 1 standardized each source table, deduplicated on clinically meaningful event keys, temporally aggregated each source independently to the patient level, and merged the per-table summaries into unique patient rows.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Stage 1 builds a single patient-level table from the EHR source tables: (1) standardizes each table ...; (2) deduplicates each table on a clinically meaningful event key; (3) temporally aggregates each source to the patient level independently; (4) Merges per-table summaries into unique patient rows.

canonical_statement: String fields were whitespace-normalized, empty strings and literal nan tokens converted to null, patient identifiers uppercased, and EHR-style datetimes converted to a unified ISO representation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: String columns were whitespace-collapsed and trimmed, empty strings and literal "nan" tokens were converted to null, and patient identifiers were uppercased ... EHR-style datetime fields ... were parsed into a unified ISO representation.

canonical_statement: Deduplication was performed before aggregation using source-specific clinically meaningful event keys to prevent repeated exports or retransmitted records from inflating counts.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each table was deduplicated using clinically meaningful event keys to prevent repeated exports or reorders from inflating counts. ... Deduplication preceded aggregation so that ... records were not double counted.

canonical_statement: Each event source was collapsed to the patient level with counts, first/latest event timestamps, and clinically relevant flags before sources were merged.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each source was collapsed to the patient level first, computing counts, first and latest event timestamps, and clinically relevant flags.

canonical_statement: Ejection-fraction ranges were parsed into low, high, and midpoint values; lowest, highest, and most-recent EF were computed, and latest-recording conflicts were flagged.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each entry was parsed into a low bound, a high bound, and a midpoint ("20–25%" becomes 20, 25, and 22.5), from which the lowest, highest, and most-recent EF were computed, plus a flag for latest recordings with conflicting values.

canonical_statement: Continuous measurements received availability indicators and missing values were preserved rather than imputed to zero.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On merging, every continuous measurement (EF, BNP, troponin, BMI, blood pressure) received an availability indicator, and missing values were kept missing rather than set to zero.

canonical_statement: Behavioral exposures were encoded as ordered categories rather than binary flags.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Behavioral exposures were kept as ordered categories rather than binary flags, because cardiovascular risk from tobacco and alcohol persists after cessation and varies by intensity.

canonical_statement: Heart-failure phenotype signals were determined from ICD-derived values rather than diagnosis names, with a conflict flag when the two sources disagreed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The heart-failure phenotype was dictated by ICD-derived values rather than diagnosis names, carrying a conflict flag when the two disagreed.

canonical_statement: The versioned scoring rubric was initially assembled by Qwen 2.5-1.5B-Instruct from recent guideline-level literature, then reviewed and approved in full by a professional cardiologist; the final version included 22 references from 2023 onward.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The rubric was developed using Qwen 2.5-1.5B-Instruct, which assembled recent guideline-level literature into a proposed scoring framework. A professional cardiologist then reviewed and approved the rubric in full. The final version included 22 references from 2023 onward.

canonical_statement: Rubric point values were an interpretable engineering design informed by clinical literature rather than quantities directly derived from published studies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The assigned point values represent an interpretable engineering design informed by clinical literature rather than quantities directly derived from published studies.

canonical_statement: Seven point-based composite categories sum component points, cap totals at 100, and map scores to high at >=55, medium at 25–54, and low below 25.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each feature sums component points, caps the total at 100, and maps the score to an ordinal label. Scores of 55 or above are classified as high, 25 to 54 as medium, and below 25 as low.

canonical_statement: Heart-failure phenotype used numeric EF when available: HFrEF at midpoint <=40, HFmrEF below 50, and HFpEF otherwise; when EF was unavailable, ICD-10 diagnosis codes were used without imputing an EF value.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: When numeric EF is present, it directly determines the phenotype: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) at midpoint ≤ 40, heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) below 50, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) otherwise. When EF is unavailable, the pipeline uses ICD-10 diagnosis codes ... without imputing an EF value.

canonical_statement: Every candidate composite-feature row was audited locally by Qwen 2.5-1.5B-Instruct, which could modify only whitelisted numeric/categorical fields; evidence JSON and explanation fields were protected.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each candidate row is audited by Qwen 2.5-1.5B-Instruct. ... Only whitelisted numeric and categorical fields may be modified ... fields ending in _json or _explanation are protected to preserve deterministic evidence traces and rationales.

canonical_statement: Unparseable LLM-auditor responses were logged as audit failures and left the original deterministic scores unchanged.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Corrections are type-coerced before application, while unparseable responses are logged as audit failures and leave the original scores unchanged.

canonical_statement: Comorbid-condition discovery used 13 fixed rubric candidates; the model selected evidence-bearing final-dataset columns but could not add conditions, invent columns, or label patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Candidate conditions are fixed in the rubric (13 cardiovascular and comorbid conditions ...), so the stage selects supporting evidence rather than discovering new conditions. ... The model cannot add conditions, invent columns, or label patients.

canonical_statement: The automated QA harness checked unique patient IDs/joins, mutually exclusive HF phenotype indicators, missing-value preservation, rubric compliance, expected monotonic behavior, traceability, and provenance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The harness verifies: (1) unique patient identifiers and valid table joins; (2) valid and mutually exclusive heart-failure phenotype indicators; (3) preservation of missing values; (4) compliance with the scoring rubric ...; (5) expected scoring behavior ...; (6) complete traceability ...; and (7) provenance ...

canonical_statement: Downstream HFrEF and HFpEF classifiers used XGBoost and compared cleaned/merged structured variables with a feature set additionally containing the composite features.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For each task, we compared a baseline containing only cleaned and merged structured variables with an aggregated feature set that additionally included the composite features. XGBoost was chosen because it natively handles missing values during split selection, eliminating explicit imputation.

canonical_statement: Model evaluation used 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated 10 times with independent shuffles, reusing the same fold assignments across paired feature-set comparisons and reporting mean plus/minus standard deviation for accuracy, AUROC, and F1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Models were evaluated using 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated 10 times with independent shuffles (50 test evaluations per model). The same fold assignments were reused for both feature sets within each task ... We report mean ± standard deviation for accuracy, AUROC, and F1 score across test folds.

canonical_statement: Global feature contributions were quantified using TreeSHAP.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Feature contributions were quantified using global TreeSHAP values.

canonical_statement: Construct validity was evaluated for every engineered rubric component by Claude Opus 4.8 using a five-dimensional rubric covering external evidence support, methodological soundness, reproducibility, and EHR data reliability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To assess feature quality beyond predictive performance, we performed a structured construct-validity evaluation of every engineered rubric component using Claude Opus 4.8 and a five-dimensional rubric. The evaluation assessed external evidence support, methodological soundness, reproducibility, and EHR data reliability.

canonical_statement: The study included an ablation analysis and an independent comparator in which an LLM engineered features directly from the raw EHR data.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We conducted two additional analyses: an ablation study measuring the contribution of individual feature categories and rubric design choices, and an independent comparator where an LLM engineered features directly from raw EHR data.

canonical_statement: Eight ablation configurations were applied independently to the full feature-engineering pipeline and evaluated using the identical XGBoost and cross-validation pipeline as the full aggregated model.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Eight targeted modifications were applied independently to the full feature-engineering pipeline ... evaluated using the identical XGBoost training and cross-validation pipeline as the full aggregated model.

canonical_statement: Ablation significance was assessed with the corrected resampled paired t-test of Nadeau and Bengio to account for correlation among repeated cross-validation folds.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Because repeated-CV folds reuse the same patients under different partitions ... significance is assessed with the corrected resampled paired t-test of Nadeau and Bengio (2003) ...

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that the results demonstrate the feasibility of automated, auditable feature engineering for complex cardiovascular EHR data.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: These results demonstrate the feasibility of automated, auditable feature engineering for complex cardiovascular EHR data, though evaluation was limited to a single-institution cohort and external validation is needed.

canonical_statement: The authors stated that the framework should remain an evidence-linked feature-engineering layer for research and clinical review rather than autonomous clinical decision-making until broader validation is completed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Until such validation, the pipeline should remain an evidence-linked feature-engineering layer for research and clinical review rather than autonomous clinical decision-making.

canonical_statement: The pipeline was evaluated on a dummy, single-institution cohort of 500 patients, limiting statistical power and external generalizability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The pipeline was evaluated on a dummy, single-institution cohort of 500 patients, limiting statistical power and external generalizability.

canonical_statement: HFrEF and HFpEF were classified against phenotype-unknown heart-failure patients rather than non-heart-failure controls, so the reported performance evaluates phenotype characterization within an HF cohort rather than general disease detection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: HFrEF and HFpEF were classified against phenotype-unknown patients rather than non-HF controls, so performance reflects phenotype characterization within an HF cohort rather than general disease detection.

canonical_statement: Evaluation emphasized internal consistency, traceability, and downstream classification rather than external clinical validity.
